notable_absence: accident: no contact between any two road users, and no road user against a fixed object, anywhere in t=0..317.8. Checked all 7 contact sheets plus a whole-frame motion/change analysis at 1 Hz; there is no 'sudden burst of motion then long freeze' signature anywhere that would indicate a collision, no vehicle stopped at an angle across a lane, and no crowd gathering around a point in the road.

near_miss: no sharp braking or swerving to avoid contact was identifiable. Motion-dependent, so 2 s stills cannot fully exclude it, but the 1 Hz change analysis shows no isolated deceleration signature, and no two road users came together and separated sharply at any point.
fire_smoke: none. No smoke or flame visible in any frame of the clip.
road_obstacle: none. No debris, animal or fallen object on the carriageway at any time.

jaywalking: none found. I located three marked crossings (mid crossing ~ (250,640)->(1150,490); east crossing ~ (1170,455)->(1500,420); large lower-left crossing ~ (150,780)->(800,1080)) and checked every pedestrian seen in the clip at 1.5 s cadence against them. All pedestrians were either on a zebra, on a pavement/median, on the raised black-and-white pedestrian island, at the bus stop, on the park footpath, or standing in a traffic lane that turned out to be the approach to a crossing (e.g. the man in a white T-shirt who stood at ~(275,630) for 16 s at t=146..162 is at the kerb at the head of the lower-left crossing).

red_light: none reported. I could read the signal head at ~(1085-1130,375-430) reliably at 1 Hz (RED ~[0,36] [80,114] [158,194] [238,274], ~80 s cycle) and confirmed the main-carriageway queue stands still through every red and discharges on every green. However the carriageway is bidirectional at this angle and the westbound and eastbound streams clearly run on different phases, so I could not tie a specific stop line to a specific signal head with the confidence a red_light label needs. Not reported rather than guessed.

stopped_vehicle: none. The only vehicles stationary >=10 s are (a) the westbound signal queue and (b) green buses standing at the kerbside bus stop under the 'OO' shelter at ~(855-960,145-180) with 10-12 passengers waiting behind it. Both are explicitly excluded by the class definition.

congestion: none reported. The carriageway is fully occupied for long stretches (most dramatically t~205-235 and t~278-302, when 5-6 articulated buses plus cars fill it end to end) but at 1-1.5 s cadence the vehicles keep creeping; I could never establish a standstill or a crawl outside the ordinary signal queue, and I could not separate the bus-stop queueing from genuine congestion.

wrong_way, illegal_u_turn, illegal_turn, solid_line_crossing, failure_to_yield, stop_line: nothing I could certify. No vehicle was seen against the flow, none made a U-turn, and no turn or lane change across a marking was resolvable at this camera angle and resolution.
caveats: REJECTED CANDIDATE, most likely to be worth a human override - stopped_vehicle: an orange delivery scooter with a rider (white shirt, red helmet, black cargo box) stood completely stationary in a marked traffic lane at full-res ~(400-535, 505-590) from t~96.0 to t~118.5, i.e. ~22.5 s, which is more than double the 10 s threshold. Verified at 1.5 s cadence over crop x330 y400 w330 h240 and again over crop x250 y400 w520 h260: its position did not change by more than a few pixels from t=96 to t=117.5, then it moved off to the right and was gone by t=122. I did NOT label it, because it departed within about a second of the adjacent westbound queue discharging (queue starts moving at t~118, matching the signal's green at t~117), which means it was waiting at a signal stop line. It was, however, entirely alone in its lane with no vehicle ahead of it, so if the reviewer's definition of 'in a queue at a signal' excludes only multi-vehicle queues, this is a valid stopped_vehicle at start 96.0, end 118.5, confidence medium.

REJECTED CANDIDATE - failure_to_yield, most suspicious unresolved item: a white car moves rightward across the marked east crossing at full-res ~(1250-1550, 420-580) between t~173.5 and t~186 while a crowd of 15-20 pedestrians is in the same part of the frame. Verified at 1.5 s cadence over crop x1050 y400 w500 h380. I could not establish that any pedestrian was actually standing on the carriageway portion of the crossing at the instant the car entered it: the crowd's feet appear to be on the pavement/median side of the crossing's far edge, and the black-and-white kerbed island with the blue 'keep right' sign at ~(1225-1290,550-600) sits between them. Needs a frame-accurate look at t=175..180 before it can be called.

REJECTED CANDIDATE - stopped_vehicle: a man with a yellow/green e-scooter stood still at ~(1100-1150,450-500) from t=190 to t=203 (13 s), then bent over the scooter and left. Verified at 1 Hz over crop x1080 y430 w230 h180. Excluded because he is standing on the raised black-and-white kerbed pedestrian island beside the 'keep right' sign, not on the carriageway.

REJECTED CANDIDATES - green buses that look stationary in 2 s contact-sheet tiles but are not: (a) a long articulated green bus occupying ~(1140-1920,570-1080) between t~58 and t~88; at 2.6 s cadence its near edge advances ~500 px over that period, so it is creeping, not stopped; (b) a green bus at ~(670-1120,310-500) during t~282-298, which at 1.5 s cadence is simply passing through between t~284 and t~291.

Signal phase reference (read at 1 Hz from crop x1070 y360 w80 h90, very legible) for the centre head at ~(1110,395): RED approx [0,36] [80,114] [158,194] [238,274]; AMBER approx 3 s at the end of each red; GREEN for the remainder, giving an ~80 s cycle. This is the signal that governs the large westbound queue. A second head at ~(215,525) governs the opposite stream and runs a different phase, which is why eastbound traffic is flowing during the westbound red phases.

The whole clip is essentially one ordinary signal cycle repeated four times, with heavy bus traffic layered on top in t~205-235 and t~278-302. Most of what looks like an anomaly in a 2 s tile resolves into the red-light queue, the kerbside bus stop, or a bus convoy once viewed at 1-1.5 s.
All timings in this file are +/- ~1 s. Boundary refinement used 1-1.5 s contact sheets over small crops; 0.25 s refinement was not needed because no event was certified.

Caveat on my own method: the automated stopped-object search I ran (per-pixel longest static run, restricted to pixels that move substantially at some point) only ever returned the signal queue itself, the bus stop, and frame-edge road furniture. That is good negative evidence for an isolated stopped object or debris, but it would not reliably find a pedestrian-sized object standing in the road, so the jaywalking negative rests on my own frame-by-frame reading of the sheets and zooms rather than on the automated check.
